title: A piloted round flies a straight line in space from the muzzle to the body under the reticle; the story-world acceptance's Rotor-kill step passes for the first time
context: Owner's eighth brief (2026-09-14): the Rotor's misses might be an angle problem with the source of the bullets; they should go in a straight line from the barrel toward the reticle, with satisfying tracers, and hits should feel registered. Until now every tower round, piloted or not, was spawned at the muzzle's surface projection and flown along the surface at half wall height in the tangent direction toward the target, with a 2D proximity hit test; from a wall-top optic aiming down at a body the picture and the round disagreed.
outcome: spawnTowerShot takes a straightTo point: for the piloted mount the target's body centre (its position lifted 0.3 cells). A straight round keeps its own point and direction in space, advances along that line, draws its tracer at that point, is range-limited by rayToTerrain from the muzzle along the line (rock and ground stop it), and is hit-tested in space against each body's centre. On a piloted hit: a white ten-dot burst on the body, a quiet high kinetic click, and the pilot's reticle cross flashes red for 120 ms (pilot.hit). td-tab.js is 17557 lines; the budget follows. Result: scripts/browser-test.mjs --story-world passes end to end, including story-world-rotor-kill, which timed out on main and on every branch run since 2026-09-14 morning; the strip assertion now excludes the GUNSHIP button.
alternatives: Widening the hit radius alone (done earlier the same day): it did not make the step pass; the geometry was the defect.
evidence: browser-test --story-world: every step passes through story-cine-redirect, with story-world-rotor-kill and story-world-fodder green; --sentry-pilot passes; npm test 103; npm run check; npm run architecture with the budget at 17557.
